RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

An all-woman panel is not evidence of anything on its own. Panels skew by department, availability and seniority; four people is a tiny sample, and women hire men constantly. Raising it makes composition your argument, which is easy to dismiss and marks you as someone who reads bias into neutral facts — damaging if you stay at the firm.

Your real grievance is procedural: a two-week-old unanswered request for written reasons. Chase that in writing, to HR and the hiring manager, citing their own policy and any statutory right to feedback.

Also weigh the substance soberly: "excellent client relationships" is a genuine leadership criterion, and a group-head role may value business development over your extra seven years of design work.
